facts.statement: Sinocalliopteryx was a carnivorous theropod dinosaur that lived in China during the Lower Cretaceous period, approximately 124.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Sinocalliopteryx (meaning 'Chinese beautiful feather') is a genus of carnivorous coelurosaurian theropod dinosaurs from the Lower Cretaceous Yixian Formation of China (Jianshangou Beds, dating to 124.6 Ma).

facts.statement: The species Sinocalliopteryx gigas was first named and described in 2007 by a team of four researchers.
facts.quote: The type species Sinocalliopteryx gigas was named and described in 2007 by Ji Shu'an, Ji Qiang, Lü Junchang and Yuan Chongxi.

facts.statement: The original fossil specimen was found at Hengdaozi in Liaoning Province, China, and dates to about 125 million years ago.
facts.quote: The holotype, JMP-V-05-8-01, was discovered at Hengdaozi, in Sihetun, in Liaoning Province, from the Jianshangou Beds of the Yixian Formation dating from the Barremian-Aptian, about 125 million years old.

facts.statement: A second, larger specimen of Sinocalliopteryx was discovered and described in 2012.
facts.quote: In 2012 a second specimen was described, CAGS-IG-T1, of an individual larger than the holotype.

facts.statement: The original 2007 specimen of Sinocalliopteryx was the largest known member of the Compsognathidae family, measuring 2.37 meters in length.
facts.quote: In 2007, the type specimen was the largest known compsognathid exemplar, at 2.37 m in length.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen measured 237 centimeters in length and was estimated to weigh twenty kilograms.
facts.quote: The preserved length of the holotype specimen is 237 centimetres. Its weight was estimated by Gregory S. Paul in 2010 at twenty kilogrammes.

facts.statement: Sinocalliopteryx was a bipedal predator.
facts.quote: Sinocalliopteryx was a bipedal predator.

facts.statement: Sinocalliopteryx had short arms with a short humerus and an ulna featuring a weakly developed olecranon process.
facts.quote: The arm had a short humerus and also the lower arm was short and elegant with an ulna showing only a weakly developed olecranon process on its back upper end.

facts.statement: The hands of Sinocalliopteryx were very elongated, reaching a length equal to the combined length of the ulna and upper arm.
facts.quote: The hand was very elongated though, as long as the ulna and upper arm combined.

facts.statement: The second claw on Sinocalliopteryx's hand was as long as the thumb claw.
facts.quote: The second claw was elongated, as long as the thumb claw.

facts.statement: The longest protofeathers on Sinocalliopteryx measured up to ten centimeters in length.
facts.quote: These longest protofeathers measured up to ten centimeters (4 in) in length.

facts.statement: Protofeathers were also preserved on the metatarsus, or upper part of the foot, of Sinocalliopteryx.
facts.quote: Protofeathers were also found on the metatarsus (upper part of the foot).

facts.statement: The original researchers assigned Sinocalliopteryx to the family Compsognathidae.
facts.quote: Sinocalliopteryx was by its describers assigned to the Compsognathidae.

facts.statement: A 2024 study by Andrea Cau questioned the classification of Sinocalliopteryx within the Compsognathidae family.
facts.quote: In 2024, Andrea Cau published a study on the phylogenetics of Compsognathids that called the assessment of Sinocalliopteryx into question.

facts.statement: Recent analyses suggest Sinocalliopteryx may belong to a group called Sinosauropterygidae rather than Compsognathidae.
facts.quote: Their phylogenetic analyses are reproduced below:

facts.statement: The holotype skeleton contained a preserved dromaeosaurid leg inside its abdominal cavity, suggesting it preyed on smaller dinosaurs.
facts.quote: The well-preserved skeleton of the Sinocalliopteryx holotype contained the partial leg of a dromaeosaurid within the abdominal cavity, comprising a complete lower leg and foot with toes and claws in their natural, articulated position.

facts.statement: Remains of at least two Confuciusornis sanctus birds were found in the second specimen, indicating it ate birds.
facts.quote: Disarticulated bones were found, in front of the lower ischia, identified as belonging to at least two individuals of Confuciusornis sanctus

facts.statement: A 13.5-centimetre scapula from a 1.5-metre-long herbivorous ornithischian was found in the second specimen.
facts.quote: a 13.5 centimetres long scapula was discovered, belonging to some 1.5 metres (4.9 ft) long herbivorous ornithischian

facts.statement: Sinocalliopteryx is the largest compsognathid discovered so far, reaching over 2 metres in length.
facts.quote: Al alcanzar más de 2m de largo, el Sinocalliopteryx es el compsognátido más grande hasta ahora descubierto.

facts.statement: Sinocalliopteryx reached a length of 2.37 metres, making it a relatively large compsognathid.
facts.quote: Considerado relativamente un compsognátido "gigante", el Sinocalliopteryx llegó a medir 2,37m de longitud.

facts.statement: The skull was up to 29 centimetres long and featured numerous serrated, conical teeth in the premaxillae and curved teeth in the maxillae.
facts.quote: El cráneo, que a su vez era grande en proporción al cuerpo, medía hasta 29cm de largo y disponía de numerosos dientes aserrados, cónicos en los premaxilares y curvados en los maxilares.

facts.statement: Most of the body was covered in well-developed protofeathers from the back of the skull to the tail tip, including the metatarsal area.
facts.quote: La mayoría del cuerpo estaba cubierto de protoplumas bien desarrolladas, desde la parte trasera del cráneo hasta la punta de la cola, llegando incluso a cubrir la zona metatarsal.

facts.statement: The second finger was the longest of the three, while the third finger was the shortest.
facts.quote: De sus tres dedos el más largo era el segundo, en contraste con el tercero, que era el más corto.

facts.statement: Sinocalliopteryx lived during the early Cretaceous, approximately 130 million years ago in the Barremian stage, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: Sinocalliopteryx gigas es la única especie conocida del género extinto Sinocalliopteryx (gr. "pluma hermosa de China") de dinosaurios terópodo compsognátido que vivió a principios del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 130millones de años, en el Barremiense, en lo que hoy es Asia.

facts.statement: Fossils were found in Liaoning province, northeast China.
facts.quote: Encontrado en la provincia de Liaoning, al noreste de China.

facts.statement: Sinocalliopteryx is classified within the family Compsognathidae.
facts.quote: familia: Compsognathidae

facts.statement: Sinocalliopteryx is considered the last member of the family Compsognathidae to be discovered.
facts.quote: El Sinocalliopteryx es considerado dentro de la familia Compsognathidae, siendo el último miembro en descubrirse.

facts.statement: Recent analyses suggest Sinocalliopteryx is phylogenetically closer to Guanlong, Proceratosaurus, and Mirischia than originally thought.
facts.quote: Aunque originalmente era relacionado con el Huaxiagnathus y el Sinosauropteryx, un análisis más reciente sugiere una posición filogenética cerca del Guanlong, Proceratosaurus y Mirischia.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Sinocalliopteryx and related genera should be placed within Tyrannosauroidea despite being closer to birds than tyrannosauroids.
facts.quote: Estos géneros (incluyendo al Sinocalliopteryx), a pesar de ser más cercanos a las aves que a los tiranosauroides, podrían ser ubicados dentro de Tyrannosauroidea hasta que nuevos estudios lo comprueben.

facts.statement: The holotype was excavated in Hengdaozi, Sihetun locality, Beipiao, west Liaoning province.
facts.quote: El holotipo fue excavado en Hengdaozi, en la localidad Sihetun de Beipiao, oeste de la provincia de Liaoning.

facts.statement: The generic name combines the prefix Sino (ancient name for China) with Greek words meaning 'beautiful' and 'wing'.
facts.quote: El nombre genérico proviene de la combinación del prefijo Sino (un nombre antiguo para China) con las palabras griegas callio ("hermoso") y pteryx ("ala").

facts.statement: The specific epithet gigas means 'giant' and refers to its large size compared to relatives.
facts.quote: El epíteto específico gigas significa "gigante" y hace referencia a su gran tamaño en comparación a sus parientes.

facts.statement: Researchers suggested the preserved prey leg indicates Sinocalliopteryx preyed on smaller, bird-like dinosaurs.
facts.quote: Ji and colleagues in 2007 suggested that this could indicate it preyed upon the smaller, bird-like dinosaur.

facts.statement: The stones in the abdomen were interpreted as gastroliths similar to those found in other theropods.
facts.quote: The authors interpreted these as gastroliths (gizzard stones) similar to those found with Nqwebasaurus and Baryonyx.

facts.statement: Despite the presence of gastroliths, no special gizzard would have been present in Sinocalliopteryx.
facts.quote: In any case no special gizzard would have been present.

facts.statement: The capture of multiple birds suggests Sinocalliopteryx may have specialized in bird prey.
facts.quote: That the second specimen in a short period of time caught two birds, together with the bird feather remains in the holotype stomach, might be an indication that Sinocalliopteryx specialised in such prey.

facts.statement: Sinocalliopteryx was likely a ground-dwelling predator that could catch birds using stealth attacks.
facts.quote: Sinocalliopteryx was in all likelihood cursorial, or ground-dwelling, and yet apparently quite capable of catching birds, e.g. by using stealth attack, a method employed by many modern cursorial predators of fowl.

facts.statement: The postcranial skeleton shows few remarkable differences from other compsognathids.
facts.quote: El esqueleto postcraneal no presenta diferencias muy remarcables con el de otros compsognátidos.

facts.statement: The vertebral column consisted of 11 cervical, 12 dorsal, and 49 caudal vertebrae, with an unknown number of sacral vertebrae.
facts.quote: La columna vertebral estaba compuesta de 11vértebras cervicales, 12dorsales y 49caudales, con una cantidad desconocida de sacrales.

facts.statement: Cervical and dorsal ribs were fine and elongated, with dorsal ribs having twelve pairs of ventral ribs (gastralia) underneath.
facts.quote: Sus costillas tanto cervicales como dorsales eran finas y prolongadas, distinguiéndose estas últimas por presentar debajo doce pares de costillas ventrales (gastralia).

facts.statement: Like Huaxiagnathus, Sinocalliopteryx had a notable furcula, supporting the presence of this bone in compsognathids.
facts.quote: Al igual que en el Huaxiagnathus, era también notable la presencia de una fúrcula, siendo una prueba más para la aparición de este hueso en compsognátidos.

facts.statement: The forelimbs extended to half the length of the hindlimbs, ending in unusually long hands comparable in size to the humerus plus radius.
facts.quote: Las extremidades superiores se extendían hasta la mitad de las extremidades inferiores, terminando en "manos" peculiarmente largas cuyo tamaño era comparable al del húmero más el radio.

facts.statement: The leg bones were somewhat robust, with a femur measuring 90% of the tibia's length.
facts.quote: Los huesos de las patas eran algo robustos, con un fémur que mide el 90% de la longitud de la tibia.

facts.statement: Sinocalliopteryx was a bipedal dinosaur with a slender build that balanced using a long tail.
facts.quote: El Sinocalliopteryx era un dinosaurio bípedo, de contextura delgada, que se balanceaba con ayuda de una larga cola.

facts.statement: A dromaeosaurid leg and four gastroliths were found inside the abdominal cavity of Sinocalliopteryx.
facts.quote: Esto se reafirma a partir del hallazgo de una pata de dromeosáurido y cuatro gastrolitos hallados dentro de su cavidad abdominal.

facts.statement: The tibia of the preserved dromaeosaurid leg fragment measured 15.5 cm in length.
facts.quote: Tan solo la tibia (de 15,5cm) era muy larga en comparación a la altura de la cavidad abdominal.

facts.statement: Protofeathers covered the back of the skull, neck, back, hips, tail, and parts of the limbs in Sinocalliopteryx.
facts.quote: Una cobertura de protoplumas recorría la parte trasera del cráneo, el cuello, la espalda, la cadera, la cola y algunas partes en las extremidades.

facts.statement: The protofeathers were longest on the hips, the base of the tail, and the rear portions of the femur.
facts.quote: Su longitud variaba en distintas partes del cuerpo, resultando más largas las que se encuentran en la cadera, la base de la cola, y las porciones traseras del fémur.

facts.statement: Protofeathers on the metatarsal area indicate they evolved in basal coelurosaurs before advanced feathered maniraptorans.
facts.quote: La presencia de protoplumas en la zona metatarsal demuestra que estas aparecieron primero en grupos celurosaurianos mucho más basales que en los avanzados manirráptores emplumados.

facts.statement: The flora of Sinocalliopteryx's habitat included conifers such as pines and araucarias.
facts.quote: Coníferas tales como pinos y araucarias comprendían la flora de este ambiente.

facts.statement: Sinocalliopteryx is the largest coelurosaur of the famous Jehol fauna, whose fossils are preserved in the Yixian and Jiufotang formations.
facts.quote: El Sinocalliopteryx es el celurosaurio más grande de la célebre fauna de Jehol, de la cual sus fósiles se preservan hoy en día en las formaciones de Yixian y Jiufotang.

facts.statement: The parent group of Sinocalliopteryx is Compsognathidae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Compsognathidae

facts.statement: Sinocalliopteryx belongs to the family Compsognathidae.
facts.quote: Family: Compsognathidae

facts.statement: Sinocalliopteryx is classified in the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: Sinocalliopteryx lived during the Barremian to Aptian stages, from 125.77 to 119.57 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Aptian (125.77 to 119.57 million years ago)

facts.statement: There are two recorded fossil occurrences of Sinocalliopteryx in the Paleobiology Database.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 2
